_what: Per-task writer instructions for ISMS-F, read by gen-grounded-items.mjs and printed as the LAST instruction in the writer prompt. A ruling about what a task is ABOUT belongs here rather than in a code edit, and the tasks carrying a note are listed at the top of every run.
_why_this_file_exists: Task 5.6 maps to ISO/IEC 17021-1, and the easy half of that standard to write from is certification-body internal procedure -- who signs what, how a mark may be printed, who decides a suspension. Six of the nine R6 rejects were exactly that. The map cannot express the distinction because the source is correct; only the angle is wrong.
_added_PROMPT_121_s3: Three tasks produced almost nothing in R7 and the cause was the SOURCE, not the round: 1.6 on NIST AI RMF survived 0 of 8 with clause-exists failing 6 (the writer invented NIST addresses), 5.5 on 17021-1 survived 0 of 6 on verbatim, and 2.3 on the Amd1:2024 climate amendment survived 1 of 8 on verbatim. Each gets a note rather than a code change.

1.6.instruction: Cite only the clause addresses listed with the passages, EXACTLY as written -- for example "MANAGE 4.3", "MAP 5.1". Never invent an address, never abbreviate one, and never convert one into ISO-style numbering. In R7 six of eight items were refused because the address cited did not exist.

1.7.instruction: Classifying an AI security concern rests on guidance: 27002 7.1 and 8.15, NIST AI RMF MANAGE 4.3, and 42001 A.6 where it matches. Guidance anchors are valid for a Foundation certification, but an item must never say 27001 or 42001 REQUIRES what guidance only recommends.

2.3.instruction: The amendment adds ONE consideration: whether climate change is a relevant issue (4.1), and that relevant interested parties can have climate-related requirements (4.2). Test that, in a scenario, quoting the amended sentences exactly. There is nothing else in the amendment to test.

5.5.instruction: Test what a CERTIFIED ORGANIZATION needs to understand about the certification cycle -- the initial audit in two stages, surveillance, recertification, suspension and withdrawal -- from the client's side. Never certification-body internals: who inside the body decides, signs or reviews something is out of scope for this task however well it is anchored.

5.6.instruction: Test what a certified organization or its customers need to understand about certification -- the scope of a certificate, what may and may not be claimed, accreditation, surveillance -- NOT certification-body internal procedure. An item about who inside the certification body signs, decides or reviews something is out of scope for this task, however well it is anchored.

cert_notes:
NEVER NAME ISO/IEC 27000 IN A SERVED FIELD (ruled PROMPT-115 s3):

- Not in the stem, not in an option, not in the explanation. Not "the 27000 family" either.
- ANCHORING THERE IS FINE. Say "the ISMS vocabulary", or "the guidance on risk", or simply state the
  definition in our own words. A gate refuses the item otherwise, and in R2 it cost 17 of 21
  rejections -- every one of them an item that was otherwise sound.

WHAT CLAUSE 9.1 ITEMS TEST (ruled PROMPT-115 s3.5):

- Test what clause 9.1 asks the ORGANIZATION TO DO -- what to monitor, when, by whom, and that the
  results are comparable and reproducible.
- Do NOT test measurement terminology: measurement method, measurement function, base measure,
  indicator, subjective versus objective. That is ISO/IEC 27004 taxonomy and it is too obscure for a
  Foundation candidate.
_cert_notes_what: Ruled PROMPT-126 s2. These two blocks lived in gen-grounded-items' WRITER_SYSTEM, so every certification was told ISMS-F's rulings -- the PROMPT-125 s5 dry run printed 'too obscure for a FOUNDATION candidate' into an ISMS-IA prompt, which is how it was noticed. Moved here VERBATIM: the before/after prompt diff for ISMS-F shows the same lines in a new position and nothing else. AIMS-F's prompt LOSES them, which is the point -- they were never AIMS-F's rulings. AIMS-F is live and complete, so no AIMS-F generation depends on them; if a future round needs the 9.1 block, copy it into TASK-WRITER-NOTES-AIMSF.json rather than back into the shared prompt.
